title: A bouncy antenna
summary: Give an antenna on a moving head a springy sway with the Jiggle behavior, working through layer parenting.

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text:
Secondary motion, the follow-through of loose parts, makes animation feel alive. The Jiggle behavior adds it for you: the part sways and bounces on a spring as whatever carries it moves.

Here the Antenna layer is parented to the Head, which runs across the stage and back.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. The antenna stays stiff as a pole.

steps.title: Select the antenna
steps.text: Press Enter again to stop. Press Home to go back to frame 1, then press V and click the antenna.

steps.title: Open the Behaviors panel
steps.text: Choose Window > Behaviors if it is not showing. It lists what is on the selection and the settings of each.

steps.title: Play it
steps.text: Press Enter, or click the play button in the timeline header. As the head starts, the antenna lags behind; as it stops, the antenna swings on past and settles.

steps.title: Make it springier
steps.text: Press Enter again to stop. Set Bounce to 85 for a wobblier antenna, or Springiness to 1 for a slow, heavy sway. Play again to see.

steps.title: Well done
steps.text:
You added follow-through with one behavior. It points says which way the part sticks out from its pivot: Down for a hanging sign or earrings. Jiggle follows its own keys as well as the layers it is parented to.

As with any behavior, Bake turns it into keyframes.
